name: Chlamydia
description: A common sexually transmitted infection caused by Chlamydia trachomatis.
riskFactors: Sexual contact with an infected partner
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation and testing when symptoms occur or after potential exposure to chlamydia.

name: Gonorrhea
anatomicalSite: Genital tract, rectum, throat, and eyes
description: A sexually transmitted infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
riskFactors: Sexual contact with an infected partner
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation and testing when gonorrhea is suspected.

name: Syphilis
anatomicalSite: Skin, mucous membranes, nervous system, cardiovascular system, and multiple organs
description: A sexually transmitted infection caused by Treponema pallidum that progresses through distinct clinical stages if untreated.
keySymptoms: Characteristic rash involving the palms or soles
riskFactors: Sexual contact with an infected partner
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical testing and treatment promptly when syphilis is suspected or exposure has occurred.

name: Trichomoniasis
description: A sexually transmitted infection caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.
whenToSeekCare: Seek testing and treatment when symptoms occur or after exposure to an infected partner.

name: Genital Herpes
anatomicalSite: Genital and perianal skin and mucous membranes
description: A sexually transmitted infection caused primarily by herpes simplex virus type 2 or type 1.
riskFactors: Sexual contact with an infected person
Previous exposure to herpes simplex virus
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for new genital blisters or ulcers, particularly during a first episode.

name: Human Papillomavirus Infection
anatomicalSite: Genital tract, anus, mouth, and throat
description: A common viral infection transmitted through intimate skin-to-skin and sexual contact; some types cause genital warts while others can cause cancers.
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for persistent genital lesions and follow recommended HPV vaccination and screening programs.

name: HIV Infection
description: A chronic viral infection caused by human immunodeficiency virus that progressively damages the immune system without effective treatment.
whenToSeekCare: Seek HIV testing after a potential exposure and medical care for symptoms suggestive of HIV infection.

name: Chancroid
description: A sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by Haemophilus ducreyi that produces painful genital ulcers.
riskFactors: Sexual contact with an infected partner
whenToSeekCare: Seek medical evaluation for painful genital ulcers or swollen groin lymph nodes.

name: Lymphogranuloma Venereum
anatomicalSite: Genital tract, rectum, and lymphatic system
description: A sexually transmitted infection caused by specific invasive strains of Chlamydia trachomatis.
riskFactors: Sexual contact with an infected partner
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical evaluation for persistent genital lesions, rectal symptoms, or unexplained groin swelling.

name: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
anatomicalSite: Uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries, and pelvic structures
etiology: Usually ascending bacterial infection, commonly associated with Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae
description: An infection and inflammation of the upper female reproductive tract that can develop as a complication of untreated sexually transmitted infections.
whenToSeekCare: Seek prompt medical assessment for pelvic pain, abnormal discharge, or fever because untreated pelvic inflammatory disease can cause serious reproductive complications.
